title: 第一章 拜占庭共和国导论

zh: “政治意识形态”这个术语在拜占庭学领域中被经常使用，而且关于它究竟是什么，学界几乎有着普遍的共识：拜占庭政治意识形态由对皇帝统治的神权式解释构成，例如自优西比乌以降的帝国颂辞中所见的那套解释，并在宫廷的头衔与仪式中得到呼应。按照这种解释，皇帝由上帝任命来统治，并有责任在其统治方式上效法或服从上帝。然而，几乎没有拜占庭学者解释他们所谓“意识形态”一词究竟何指，或把它置于某种特定的理论进路之中。
通常，这个术语只是被用来意指“一套基本信念”，其预设是帝国中的大多数人都持有这些信念，从而默然同意了帝国体制。但至今没有人证明过民众
接受了宫廷文学的那些神权观念，也没有人证明过他们
接受，更没有任何方法论被设计出来以产生这样的证明。
en: The term “political ideology” is used regularly in the field of Byzantine Studies and there is a nearly universal consensus about what it was: Byzantine political ideology consisted of the theocratic interpretation of imperial rule found, for example, in imperial panegyrics from Eusebios onward and was echoed in the titles and ceremonies of the court. According to this interpretation, the emperor was appointed to rule by God and had a responsibility to imitate or obey God in his manner of rule. Almost no Byzantinists, however, explain what they mean by the word “ideology” or situate it within a specific theoretical approach.

Usually, the term is used to mean just “a basic set of beliefs,” on the assumption that most people in the empire held these beliefs and thus tacitly consented to the imperial system. But no one has yet proven
or
the population accepted the theocratic notions of court literature, nor has any methodology been devised for generating such proof.

zh: 本书意在为拜占庭政治意识形态研究做出一份贡献。事实上，它首次把这个主题当作一个开放的问题来对待，而不是当作一套既定的、可供未来研究安心在其上搭建的假设。“意识形态”恰好是一个有力的术语，有着丰富的哲学史，尽管大多数历史学家已经削弱了这个词的理论锋芒，把它当作一个人或社会似乎持有的任何一套信念，无论关乎政治、社会与经济秩序、性、宗教，还是别的什么范畴。

有时信念是从历史现象（行动或制度）中推断出来的，有时则是从文本中引述出来的，而这些文本未必能充分解释那些历史现象（在拜占庭学中，意识形态大多取自文本，却很少被带入政治史的分析）。那些提出“意识形态理论”的现代理论流派，虽然丰富了这一术语的历史与语义范围，却往往彼此抵牾，而且未必适用于拜占庭材料所提出的具体问题。我对这类文献的研究，没有发现任何一个模型其益处大于其弊端。大多数理论聚焦于现代问题，通常关乎阶级斗争与激进政治、从精神分析立场出发对“自我”的建构，或某位现代思想家的思想，而且这些理论又常以难以索解的行话写成。看来在这个领域，研究前现代的历史学家仍只能自寻出路。
en: This book is meant as a contribution to the study of Byzantine political ideology. Indeed, it approaches the topic for the first time as an open question and not as a settled set of assumptions on which future research can safely be built. “Ideology” happens to be a potent term with a rich philosophical history, even though most historians use it in a domesticated sense as any set of beliefs that a person or society seems to hold, whether relating to politics, social and economic orders, sex, religion, or some other category.

Sometimes beliefs are inferred from historical phenomena (actions or institutions) and sometimes they are quoted from texts, which may or may not adequately explain those historical phenomena (in Byzantine Studies, ideology is largely drawn from texts, and it is rarely brought into the analysis of political history). While they have enriched the term’s history and semantic range, modern theoretical schools of thought that have proposed “theories of ideology” are often at odds with each other, and they are not always applicable to the specific problems posed by Byzantine material. My study of this literature has turned up no model whose benefits outweigh its disadvantages. Most theories focus on modern problems, usually relating to class struggle and radical politics, the construction of the Self from a psychoanalytic standpoint, or the thought of a modern thinker, and too much is written in code. In this area, it seems, premodern historians must still fend for themselves.

zh: 词语并没有天生的含义，“意识形态”尤其具有相当大的可塑性。我将在一种特定的意义上使用它，如果它与读者所偏好或习惯的用法不完全一致，还请读者包涵。倘若它仍然令人别扭，一个笨拙的替代说法会是：“统治者与臣民之间共享的、关于某一政治秩序之规范性层面的背景信念，有证据表明，这些信念塑造了民众在政治领域内互动的方式，尤其是在权力分配存在分歧的时期。”由于围绕权力分配的分歧正是政治的实质所在，这一定义要求理论与实践必须被结合起来研究。那么，这就可以作为意识形态的一个简明定义。在某些方面，它与流行的定义（尤其是马克思主义的定义）相重叠，但在另一些方面又与之不同。
en: Words do not have innate meanings, and “ideology” in particular is quite malleable. I will use it in a specific way and ask the reader’s indulgence if it does not correspond exactly to the one he or she prefers or is used to. If it still grates, a cumbersome substitute would be “background beliefs, shared between rulers and subjects, about the normative aspects of a given political order, which can be shown to have shaped how the population interacted within the political sphere, especially in times when there was disagreement about the allocation of power.” As disagreements over the allocation of power are the stuff of politics, this definition of ideology requires that theory and praxis be studied in tandem. That, then, may serve as a concise definition of ideology. In some respects, it overlaps with prevalent definitions, especially Marxist ones, but in other respects it differs from them.

zh: 具体而言，与今天大多数研究罗马与拜占庭的历史学家一样，我并不明确地把意识形态定义为

信念，例如定义为这样一种信念：其功能是通过使社会秩序与等级显得自然因而不可避免（或超自然因而不可避免），来为它们辩护，而事实上它们不过是与特定群体（通常是精英）的利益相连的有赖于特定条件才成立的虚构。我之所以不采用这一分析传统，部分原因在于本书所讨论的那些信念，是由一种广泛的政治共识所生成、维持和强制推行的。它们关乎国家权力的正当使用、皇帝职位的目的，以及谁有权使权力的分配与再分配合法化。一个历史学家如何能够论证这样的信念要么为真要么为假，这一点并不清楚。相比之下，倒是可以论证：皇帝由上帝任命来统治这一神权观念是虚假的，而且它确实更多地服务于宫廷的需要而非民众的需要（尽管并非仅仅如此，我们将会看到）。然而按照我的定义，那个神权观念可能一开始就够不上称为意识形态。因此，尽管某些意识形态很可能就是被普遍接受的、服务于精英利益的虚假信念（今天在我们周围、甚至在我们内心，就有许多这样的信念），但这里将要呈现的意识形态并不属于那一类型。
en: Specifically, like most historians of Rome and Byzantium today, I do not define ideology explicitly as

belief, for example, as a belief whose function was to rationalize social orders and hierarchies by making them appear natural and thus inevitable (or supernatural and thus inevitable), when in fact they were only contingent fictions linked to the interest of specific groups, usually elites. I refrain from this tradition of analysis in part because the beliefs discussed in this book were generated, maintained, and enforced by a broad political consensus. They were about the proper use of state power, the purpose of the imperial position, and who had the right to legitimate the allocation and reallocation of power. It is not clear how a historian can argue that such beliefs were either true or false. It is, by contrast, possible to argue that the theocratic notion that the emperor was appointed to rule by God was false and that it did serve the needs of the court more than those of the population (though not exclusively so, as we will see). According to my definition, however, that theocratic notion might not qualify as an ideology to begin with. Therefore, while some ideologies may well be generally accepted false beliefs that serve the interests of elites (and there are many of those all around us today, and even within us), the ideology that will be presented here will not be of that type.

zh: 流行定义与我自己的定义之间的另一个区别在于：意识形态并不总是由政治精英制造、并为政治精英的利益服务的。我将论证，拜占庭政治领域的意识形态，延续了罗马共和传统对权力从何而来、如何使用、怎样取得正当性的看法。我将提出一种自下而上的政治权威模型，以修正、乃至反驳该领域盛行的自上而下模型。顺带地，这一模型将有助于解释拜占庭政治领域的两个独特特征：为什么它能作为一个整合的、连贯的道德与政治共同体存续如此之久（比任何其他君主制都更久），以及为什么皇位之下的政治领域何以如此动荡，随时可能不再效忠皇帝。通常，这两个事实会彼此紧张，但在拜占庭的“君主制共和国”中，它们却相互强化。
en: Another difference between prevalent definitions and my own is that ideologies are not always manufactured by and for the benefit of political elites. I will be arguing that the ideology of the Byzantine political sphere represented a survival of Roman republican notions about the sources, uses, and legitimation of power. A bottom-up model of political authority will be presented to temper, even push back against, the top-down one that prevails in the field. Incidentally, this model will help to explain two unique features of the Byzantine political sphere: why it survived for so long as an integrated, coherent moral and political community (longer than any other monarchy) and why the imperial throne sat atop a political realm that was so turbulent and potentially disloyal. Ordinarily, these two facts would be in tension, but in the Byzantine “monarchical republic” they reinforced each other.

zh: 因此，意识形态在这里不会被用来指与“现实”
的“修辞”，也不会仅仅指任何一套可以被表述出来、即便并不决定政治实践的教条。

children: 意识形态必须帮助我们理解政治领域的实际运作。

zh: 一种文化的政治史，不能成为对其（所谓）主导意识形态的反驳。于是，并非所有被陈述出来的信念，都具有同样的切身分量、在认知上和政治上享有同样的存在地位，也未必获得同等程度的认可或产生同样的历史影响。本书的目标，将是辨明人们如何理解自己在社会中的位置，以及他们如何彼此互动、如何与其政治制度互动。它将试图揭示拜占庭人的一些基本观念：他们生活在何种政治社会之中，其道德逻辑是什么，什么是可接受的、什么不是；换言之，在政治上什么对他们“说得通”、什么说不通。
一位物理学家把这比作一个社会的“心理壁纸”，或“把我们平常顾不上明说的前提简要标示出来”，
一位神经科学家则把它比作“那些最根深蒂固的本能，[它们]通常被排除在探究的聚光灯之外”。
意识形态是政治文化中被视为理所当然的东西，而不仅仅是、或主要不是那些被高声地、防御性地宣称出来的东西。因此，对意识形态更充分的处理，或许根本不会在存在论上把它归类为一种
，因为信念是可以轻易改变的。“意识形态比信念更个人化（因为我们可以干脆改变自己的信念），比知识或理由更少受到自觉意识的审视，范围又超出个人。”
en: Therefore, ideology will not here be used to refer to “rhetoric”
to “reality” or simply to any set of doctrines that can be articulated even if they were not determinative of political practice.

children: Ideology must help us to understand the actual operations of the political sphere.

en: The political history of a culture cannot be a refutation of its (alleged) dominant ideology. Not all stated beliefs, then, were equivalent in terms of their existential valence, cognitive and political ontology, or the degree of their popular acceptance and historical impact. The goal of this book will be to identify how people understood their place in society and how they interacted with each other and their political institutions. It will attempt to uncover the Byzantines’ basic notions about what kind of political society they lived in, what its moral logic was, what was acceptable and what not; in other words, what “made sense” to them politically and what not.
A physicist has compared this to the “mental wallpaper” of a society or “a shorthand for the assumptions we don’t get around to articulating,”
a neuroscientist to the “most hardwired instincts [that] have usually been left out of the spotlight of inquiry.”

Ideology is what was taken for granted in the political culture and not only, or not primarily, what was loudly and defensively proclaimed. A fuller treatment of ideology, therefore, might not classify it ontologically as a type of
at all, for beliefs can be easily changed. “Ideology is more personal than belief (since we can simply change our beliefs), less conscious than knowledge or reasons, larger than the individual.”

zh: 这就把我们带到了
及其特定语境局限的问题上。尽管以“拜占庭政治意识形态”或“政治理论”为题的研究比比皆是，拜占庭人却并未以系统而全面的方式对其国家或社会进行理论化。

不太可能有哪一种体裁或哪一部文本完美地概括了政治领域的规范，因为所有文本都是在特定的历史、政治与话语语境中产生的，而且通常服务于个人或机构的特定利益。意识形态是意义与规范性的母体，但我们不应指望发现它们被摆成方便的公式。它们通常是隐含的而非显白的，是那种在政治推理行为中促成从前提过渡到结论的底层逻辑。而最说得通的东西，恰恰是最不需要被申说的东西，因为它可以被视为理所当然。意识形态必须被发掘出来；它未必是用十英尺高的金字写成的。
en: This brings us to the problem of the

and their context-specific limitations. Despite the prevalence of studies with the words “Byzantine political ideology” or “political theory” in their titles, the Byzantines did not theorize their state or society in systematic and comprehensive ways.

It is unlikely that any one genre or text perfectly encapsulated the norms of the political sphere, as all were produced within specific historical, political, and discursive contexts and usually served the particular interests of individuals or institutions. Ideologies are matrices of meaning and normativity, but we should not expect to find them laid out in convenient formulas. They are usually implicit rather than explicit, the underlying logic that facilitates the move from premise to conclusion in the act of political reasoning. And what makes the most sense is precisely what needs to be affirmed the least, as it can be taken for granted. Ideology must be excavated; it will not necessarily be written in letters of gold ten feet tall.

zh: 拜占庭史料向我们呈现了范围广泛的各种态度、乃至“信念”，它们出现在不同的场合，在特定语境中被激活，而且主要地、甚至专门地在那些语境中才具有相关性。例如，一部创新的政治论著、帝国修辞中的一个
（套语）、历史学家评判皇帝统治的标准、一篇法律序言、暴动民众在街头高喊反对某位皇帝的口号，以及一部献给皇帝的道德劝诫之作，并不都在同一层面上运作，也不都值得我们给予同等的关注。总体而言，这里提出的论证将避开拜占庭千年间产生的、如今正重新受到关注的少数原创政治思想的思辨性著作，例如六世纪匿名的
、托马斯·马吉斯特罗斯论国王及其臣民的论著，以及莫斯霍普洛斯的宣誓理论。
他们的提议或许建立在共同分享的假设之上，但我们只有通过与其它类型的证据相比较才能知道这一点。这些文本必须放在与整个政治领域的关系中来理解，但它们只是该领域某些特定方面的独特变体。它们必须在之后才被带入讨论，因为我们不能预先假定它们反映了拜占庭政体的规范。
en: The Byzantine sources present us with a wide range of attitudes and even “beliefs” that appear in different settings, were activated in specific contexts, and were relevant primarily, or even exclusively, in those contexts. For example, an innovative political treatise, a

of imperial rhetoric, the standards by which historians evaluated emperors’ reigns, a legal preface, the slogans chanted in the streets against an emperor by a rioting populace, and a work of moral advice addressed to an emperor do not all operate on the same level or have equivalent claims on our attention. In general, the argument presented here will avoid the few speculative works of original political thought that were produced during the Byzantine millennium and are now receiving renewed attention, such as the anonymous sixth-century
Thomas Magistros’s treatise on kings and their subjects, and Moschopoulos’s theory of oaths.

Their proposals may have rested on commonly shared assumptions, but we can know this only by comparison with other types of evidence. These texts have to be understood in relation to the political sphere as a whole, but they are idiosyncratic variations of particular aspects of it. They must be brought into the discussion afterward, as they cannot be assumed in advance to reflect the norms of the Byzantine polity.

zh: 无论如何，关于拜占庭意识形态的正统观点并不依赖那些论著。学者们反而抓住了“皇帝由上帝任命”这一公式，并在它出现的所有体裁中追踪它，排斥其它一切。这产生了一系列可以相互替换的观点，有些更注重法理和法律形式，有些更偏道德说教，或偏仪式，或偏神学，等等，

而它们都绝对地执着于上帝与皇帝之间的关联。但有可能我们在这里被宫廷引入了歧途。帝国理念之所以如此频繁地被重复利用，是因为它令人印象深刻、便于话语操作，而且由一个顺手的公式构成。但这恰恰就是它被设计出来的样子。上帝—皇帝这一图式的公式化性质，使它易于被重复，无论是在拜占庭还是在学术中。然而这并不意味着我们就应当轻信地透过它来看待文化的其余部分。例如，至今没有人解释过，所谓皇帝由上帝加冕（以及诸如此类）的信念，在历史进程中究竟如何影响了臣民和统治者的往来，政治史的事实也从未由它得到解释。所以我们需要保持怀疑：那些有能力广为传布消息的人最响亮的宣称，未必就是意识形态。它无疑是文化的一个重要部分，但究竟以何种方式如此，仍不清楚。我们必须改用多种多样的史料，对其政治逻辑进行“三角测量”，以搜寻一个（往往未被言说的）意识形态内核。这就是为什么我将使用尽可能广泛的史料。其结果可能并不完全连贯或有序，部分原因在于像拜占庭这样复杂的文化，没有一个是完全连贯或有序的。但它的中心维持了很长时间，而我不相信那个中心位于皇帝职位的神学之中。
en: The orthodox view of Byzantine ideology does not rest on those treatises anyway. Scholars have instead latched on to the formula that the emperor was appointed by God, and pursue it, to the exclusion of all else, through all genres in which it appears. This has resulted in a series of interchangeable views, some more legalistic, other moralizing, or ceremonial, or theological, and so on,

and they share an absolute commitment to the nexus of God and emperor. But it is possible that we have been led astray by the court here. The imperial idea is so often recycled because it is impressive, is conveniently discursive, and consists of a handy formula. But that is exactly how it was designed. The formulaic nature of the God-emperor schema makes it easily repeatable, both in Byzantium and in scholarship. This does not mean, however, that we should gullibly view the rest of the culture through it. For instance, no one has yet explained how the alleged belief that the emperor was crowned by God (and all that) shaped subject-ruler interactions in real time, nor have the facts of political history been explained by it. So we need to be skeptical: what is asserted the loudest by those who have the means to broadcast messages is not necessarily an ideology. It was an important part of the culture, no doubt, but in what way exactly remains unclear. We must instead use a variety of sources to “triangulate” their political logic in search of an (often unspoken) ideological core. That is why I will use as wide a variety of sources as possible. The result may not be entirely coherent or orderly, in part because no complex culture such as Byzantium was fully coherent or orderly. But its center held for a long time, and I do not believe that it was located in the theology of the imperial position.

zh: 拜占庭意识形态的某些方面容易辨认。所有历史学家都会同意，君主制被（几乎）普遍视为最优的政体类型。在这里所研究的时期，没有任何运动试图建立另一种政体，只有两三位理论家（在六世纪早期）青睐共和国。因此，就政治领域的存在论而言，由一个人来主事，对拜占庭人来说在直觉上是“说得通”的。然而这并不能让我们走多远。君主制是一个宽泛的范畴，会因人们对君权的来源、怎样运用才正当以及君臣关系的看法不同而呈现不同形态。那么，拜占庭是哪一种君主制？本书的论点是：拜占庭是一个共和式君主制，而主要不是一个君权神授的君主制。在本节的其余部分， 我将说明，为什么我们有理由怀疑这套神权辞令。支持这些理由的证据将在本书其余部分呈现。
en: Some aspects of Byzantine ideology are easy to identify. All historians would agree that monarchy was (nearly) universally regarded as the optimal type of regime. In the period studied here, there were no movements to institute a different regime and only two or three theorists (in the early sixth century) favored the Republic. Therefore, in terms of the ontology of the political sphere, it made intuitive “sense” to the Byzantines that one person should be in charge. Yet this does not take us far. Monarchy is a broad category that can be inflected by different ideologies concerning the source and legitimate use of its power and the relationship between ruler and subjects. What type of monarchy, then, was Byzantium? The thesis of this book is that Byzantium was a republican monarchy and not primarily a monarchy by divine right. In the rest of this section, I will set out some of the reasons that warrant skepticism of the theocratic rhetoric. The evidence for them will be presented in the rest of the book.

zh: 第一，我们目前所理解的帝国意识形态几乎只聚焦于皇帝，而对于界定他与臣民关系的原则几乎无话可说。由于那种关系没有被理论化，学者实际上把这一关系当作主要靠强制性制度维持的关系来考察。大多数声称要谈论“帝国意识形态”的研究，真正指的是
仿佛他是唯一要紧的政治实体；它们指的并不是

is fairly uncontroversial but is doubly wrong: it was not the

and the office hardly exhausted the reach and content of Byzantine political ideology. The Byzantines had a sophisticated ideological ontology that placed the office into a particular kind of relation with the rest of society, of which they also had a specific, distinctively Roman view. But this is invisible in most modern accounts, which are biased in favor of the most theological end of court propaganda and tend to omit from their discussion passages in those texts that point toward the republican dimension of political ideology, or even go so far as to quote passages in which the legitimacy of imperial rule is drawn from the
to support a view that it was bestowed by

No scholar is playing fast and loose with the evidence here, in part because no one seems to be aware that there are in fact alternatives in play here. Rather, the theological bias is so ingrained in the field that we assume that all texts must be saying the same thing, namely, what we have all instructed each other to see through sheer repetition. There is a general bias (that also permeates the study of Byzantine religion) in favor of official doctrinal positions as opposed to ideologies that are revealed in social practice or less official sources. That is, in part, why the study of religion in Byzantium is identical with the study of Orthodoxy, and why anthropology has made so little headway: we tend to privilege what the Byzantines professed to believe over what they actually did.

zh: 第二，在我们关于拜占庭意识形态的理论与拜占庭人作为历史行动者的实际行为之间，存在着一道鸿沟。如果皇帝的合法性是神学性的；如果正如西里尔·曼戈断然所说，“上帝不仅命定了帝国的存在，他还拣选了每一位个别的皇帝，这就是为什么没有为他的任命制定任何人间规则”；
而且，如果拜占庭人真如我们被引导去相信的那样正统，那么怎么会这样：他们不仅常常猛烈抨击自己的皇帝，在公开场合唱歌羞辱他们，密谋反对他们，而且还反叛他们、或加入反对他们的叛乱，进而杀死他们或弄瞎他们，而在那些时刻似乎并不记得上帝或他的命定？为什么宝座的保有如此脆弱？这一事实在关于拜占庭皇帝职位与体制的研究中很少被提及，而这种省略恰恰使所谓主导意识形态的幻觉得以成立。
因此，毫不奇怪，至今没有人能够基于“帝国意识形态”来解释拜占庭政治的动荡。在现代学术中，政治史是被实用主义地讲述的，按每位学者所理解的每一次事件中的权力消长的方式来讲。但为什么我们在描述这类事件时，要把所谓主导意识形态搁置一旁？难道不恰恰
意识形态才应当帮助我们解释它们吗？“权力动力学”与“实用主义”在大多数其它领域中都是文化特定的，但在我们书写拜占庭历史的方式中却不然，因为我们所选择的“意识形态”模型对政治领域的实际运作无话可说，使我们每个人都只能任由自己关于权力如何运作的直觉摆布。
en: Second, there is a gap between our theories of Byzantine ideology and how the Byzantines actually behaved as historical agents. If the emperor’s legitimacy was theological; if, as Cyril Mango flatly stated, “not only did God ordain the existence of the empire, He also chose each individual emperor, which was why no human rules were formulated for his appointment”;

and also, if the Byzantines were as orthodox as we have been led to believe, then how was it that they not only criticized their emperors so virulently and so commonly, sang offensive songs about them in public, and plotted against them but also rebelled against them or joined rebellions against them and then killed them or blinded them, without seeming to remember God or his ordinations at such times? Why was tenure of the throne so fragile? This fact is rarely mentioned in studies of the imperial office and system of Byzantium, an omission that enables the illusion of the alleged dominant ideology.

It is not surprising, consequently, that no one has yet been able to explain the turbulence of Byzantine politics on the basis of the “imperial ideology.” Political history is recounted pragmatically in modern scholarship, in whatever way each scholar thinks the dynamics of power played out each time. But why do we set the allegedly dominant ideology aside when we describe such events? Should it not rather be

the ideology that helps us to interpret them? “Dynamics of power” and “pragmatism” are culturally specific in most other fields, but not in how we write Byzantine history, because our chosen model of “ideology” has nothing to say about the actual operation of the political sphere, leaving us each at the mercy of his own intuitions about how power worked.

Yet upon reflection this makes sense, given that the Byzantine historians often present a picture of the polity and emperor that is at odds with what the court genres say, sometimes explicitly so, and their narratives, from which we must infer the “dynamics of power,” do not lend themselves to handy formulas; they are in fact quite complex. zh: 第三，鉴于拜占庭人就是罗马人（这对他们来说是直觉上显而易见的，即便对我们不是），任何关于他们意识形态的论述，除非认真考虑其政体的罗马基础，否则都无法成立。诸如“基督教是拜占庭帝国无所不在的意识形态，其仪式、教义与结构支配着生活的方方面面……身为拜占庭人，首先就是一名基督徒”

这样的说法，一个人越是花时间研读原始史料，就越觉得它们奇怪。它们事实上是拜占庭学这个回音室的产物，而拜占庭学出于自身的意识形态理由，顽固地把罗马的声音拒之门外。迄今为止，只有贝克公开抵制了这一趋势，并顶住了那些长久以来否认拜占庭罗马身份的政治利益（已转化为学术偏见）的压力。因此，论证的这一方面将被详细展开。“罗马”并不只是皇帝们用于宣传或外交的一个显赫名号。它是生成拜占庭政体之道德逻辑的母体。我们所谓的拜占庭，不是别的，正是一个罗马的
，一个“共和国”。其意识形态的两个特征可以在这里陈述，以表明它与帝国—神学模型的区别：其一，它设定了一个理论上世俗的政治领域，运作于皇帝与其臣民之间（说它世俗，不是因为它排斥宗教，而是因为它不由宗教所界定，宗教只是政体的一部分）。这个空间显然不同于那个中介皇帝与上帝之关系的形而上空间。其二，它确立了一种自下而上的主权模式，政治共同体中的其他成员既能够追究皇帝的责任，也确实时常这样做。
en: Third, given that the Byzantines were Romans (it was intuitively obvious to them, if not to us), no account of their ideology can stand unless it seriously considers the Roman basis of their polity. Statements such as that “Christianity was the all-pervasive ideology of the Byzantine empire, its rituals, doctrines, and structures dominating every aspect of life... In being Byzantine, one was first and foremost a Christian”

sound increasingly stranger the more time one spends with the primary sources. They are, in fact, products of the echo chamber that is Byzantine Studies, which has rigidly barred entry to the Roman voice for its own ideological reasons. So far only Beck openly resisted this trend and pushed back against the weight of political interests (turned into academic biases) that have denied the Roman identity of Byzantium for so long. This aspect of the argument will, then, be developed in detail. “Rome” was not just a prestigious name used by the emperors for propaganda or diplomacy. It was the matrix that generated the moral logic of the Byzantine polity. What we call Byzantium was nothing other than a Roman

a “republic.” Two features of its ideology can be stated here to indicate its difference from the imperial-theological model: One, it postulated a theoretically secular political sphere that operated between the emperor and his subjects (secular not in that it excluded religion but in that it was not defined by it, religion being only one part of the polity). This space was obviously not the same as the metaphysical space that mediated the relationship between emperor and God. Two, it authorized a bottom-up model of sovereignty in which the emperor could be and often was held accountable to the rest of the polity.

zh: 把拜占庭等同于某种特定类型的神权秩序，是由启蒙思想家推动的，他们想把它当作一个模型，借以间接地讨论当代问题。他们对拜占庭的历史真相并不感兴趣；它只是一个方便的模型，而他们是在为自己的政治目的使用它。近年来，有一股协调一致的努力，要抵制那个论战性模型的许多方面，但神权意识形态依然存续。要理解这是为什么并不容易。我们不再受制于这样一种观念：罗马专属于西方的、以拉丁为基础的文化与制度。相反，有可能帝国理念之所以仍被学者们推崇，恰恰是因为它与现代西方思考政治的方式格格不入。通过宣称自己接触到据称与我们自己的思维方式不可通约的“他者”思维方式，学者们可以表明自己懂得人类学的要求，并让自己和听众确信：他们通过不把现代规范投射到一种异文化之上，尊重了它的他者性。于是，让拜占庭人显得过于理性、正常、务实或诸如此类，就会是一种人类学上的失败。这变成了纲领性的东西：“拜占庭人在大多数方面都不同于现代西方文化”，最近一部论文集这样开篇，而这种做法相当常见。
我们相信这类东西的需要，大概就内建于
意识形态之中。
en: The identification of Byzantium with a particular type of theocratic order was promoted by Enlightenment thinkers who wanted to use it as a model by which to discuss contemporary problems indirectly. They were not interested in the historical truth about Byzantium; it was only a convenient model, and they were using it for their own political purposes. In recent years there has been a concerted effort to push back against many aspects of that polemical model, but the theocratic ideology abides. It is not easy to understand why this is. We are no longer beholden to the notion that Rome belongs exclusively to western, Latin-based cultures and institutions. Instead, it is possible that the imperial idea is still promoted by scholars precisely because it is alien to modern western ways of thinking about politics. By proclaiming that they are in touch with “other” ways of thinking that are allegedly incommensurate with our own, scholars can establish anthropological credentials and reassure themselves and their audiences that they are respecting the other-ness of a foreign culture by not projecting modern norms onto it. It would then be an anthropological failure to make the Byzantines seem too rational, normal, pragmatic, or whatever. This becomes programmatic: “The Byzantines were different from modern western cultures in most respects,” begins a recent collection of essays, and its approach is not untypical.
Our need to believe such things is probably built into
ideology.

我的目的也不是要把利奥作为原创思想家加以抬高或贬低，而只是要揭示他似乎视为理所当然的那些观念：关于他作为立法者相对于其所治理的政体的角色，以及他与该政体“前法律”规范性实践的辩证性互动。
en: I will take as a starting point the collection of 113 laws (technically called
in Greek,

in Latin) issued by the emperor Leon VI (886–911) in the very middle of the middle Byzantine period. These texts are not well known outside the subfield of Byzantine legal studies, and there is almost no scholarship devoted to them in English. As it has come down to us, the collection was edited and revised, probably privately, before the production of the earliest surviving manuscript, though the revision aimed only to summarize and condense the contents and eliminate the formal protocols that had in the meantime become redundant. It is likely that the original collection was made or sponsored by Leon himself, who wrote the
personally in the first years of his reign (between 886 and 889). If they were not originally issued as a single corpus, they quickly became that.
We will not be concerned here with how these

fit into the overall history and shape of Byzantine law, how they were meant to interact with prior legislation, or with their specific provisions, sources, and social impact, topics that have already been discussed by others.

Nor is it my purpose to highlight or demote Leon as an original thinker, only to bring out the notions that he seems to have taken for granted regarding his role as lawgiver in relation to the polity that he was governing and his dialectical engagement with its “pre-legal” normative practices.

zh: 第一条
开篇赞扬查士丁尼的立法工作，把它作为利奥立法工作的一个显而易见的范本。
查士丁尼协调法律的决定“对
是最有用、最卓越的”，并且“造福了臣民”，但它并不完全成功，因为混乱随着新法律的增加、以及“那些未被法律批准、却以民众意志为其唯一权威的习惯”而悄悄潜入。
利奥宣布他打算按其在序言中解释的方式重新协调法律，但他训示其官员与法官：任何习惯，除非带有他正式批准的印记，否则不得被视为具有法律约束力。换言之，习惯有权获得立法者的关注与考量，并在政体中提出一种规范性要求，但它并不具有法律约束力，除非由正当权威——即皇帝——正式把它制定为法律。
这些
紧密遵循这一纲领性陈述。在一个例子中，一项现行习惯被明确称为优于一部旧法律，并取代了它。
在另一个例子中，注意到一项难以实行的法律已被“人民的意志”（τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἡ προαίρεσις）所拒斥，因此它必须去除：其条款已经不再是
的一部分（οὐ πολιτευομένων），因此皇帝正式“把它们从

于是看来，利奥所谓的“人民的意志”，在皇帝介入之前就已经确保了这部法律在事实上（de facto）不是政体的一部分，尽管它仍具有
（法律上）的效力。这就提出了一个问题：究竟是谁构成并界定了政体。政体似乎是由皇帝与“人民”分别作出的官方与非官方决定共同构成的。
en: The first
begins by praising the legislative work of Justinian, as an obvious model for that of Leon.
Justinian’s decision to harmonize the laws was “a most useful and excellent one for the

” and worked “to the benefit of the subjects,” but it was not altogether successful as confusion crept in through the addition of new laws as well as “by customs that were not ratified by law but had as their sole authority the will of the masses.”

Leon declares his intention to reharmonize the laws in the way that he explains in the preface, but he instructs his magistrates and judges that no custom is to be considered as legally binding unless it bears the stamp of his official approval. In other words, custom has a right to the lawgiver’s attention and consideration and poses a normative claim in the polity, but it is not legally binding unless it is formally made into a law by the proper authority, that is, the emperor.
The

In another it is noted that an awkward law had been rejected by “the will of the people” (τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἡ προαίρεσις) and so it had to go: its provisions were already not part of the
(οὐ πολιτευομένων) and therefore the emperor formally “ostracized them from the

It would seem, then, that what Leon calls “the will of the people” had already ensured that this law was not de facto part of the polity before the emperor’s intervention, regardless of the fact that it still had

validity. This raises the question of who really constituted and defined the polity. The polity seems to be constituted by both official and unofficial decisions taken respectively by the emperor and “the people.”

... which was already part of the

aspect constituted by imperial ratification. Leon, as emperor, uses the imperative to do something that the people have already done. In

20, he recognizes that an attempt by his father Basileios I to revive an older law and annul recent legislation had proven futile, as the people were irrationally clinging to their customs. Rather grudgingly, he endorses their practice. He gives the impression of having been compelled to do so by the customs of the popular polity.

在
第57条中，利奥批准了一项习惯做法，注意到即便没有批准，它对“如今的人们（τοῖς νῦν）”似乎也已足够，但他仍认为它值得正式认可。在某些情况下，他以家长式的姿态复活那些已废置不用的法律，
所以我们或许可以说，皇帝与其臣民之间发生着某种“协商”。但这并不完全是利奥想要呈现的样子。他在
第59条中大发家长式议论：“法律之于公民（

但我们在上面观察到的同一种紧张在这里也适用：什么样的父亲会根据其子女正在做的事来定规矩？这里究竟谁主事？利奥想让他的听众相信主事的是他。但在大多数事务上他并没有带头。
他的明喻掩盖了、而非揭示了正在发生的事。这与一个事实相关：利奥似乎并没有坚定的标准来决定哪些“习惯”该批准、哪些不该。无论如何，有一件事是清楚的：这里的协商发生在一个“切实的人间”领域，

en: Leon alternately calls the bearers of custom “the people,” “the majority,” or “the masses” (οἱ ἄνθρωποι, τὸ πλῆθος, ὁ ὄχλος), all ways of rendering the Latin
He refers to them in a

an interesting metaphor, alluding perhaps to the ancient metaphor of the ship of state.
In

57, Leon ratifies a customary practice, noting that even without ratification it seems adequate “to people these days (τοῖς νῦν),” but still he deems it worthy of official sanction. In some cases he paternalistically revives laws that had fallen into desuetude,
so we might speak of a certain sort of “negotiation” taking place between the emperor and his subjects. But this is not exactly how Leon wanted to present it. He waxes paternalistic in
59: “The laws ought to be to citizens
what a father is to his children, looking, that is, solely to the advantage and security of those who comprise the

But the same tension that we observed above applies here too: What kind of father makes rules based on what his children are doing? Who is in charge here? Leon wants his audience to believe that it is he. But he is not taking the lead in most issues.

His simile disguises, rather than reveals, what is going on. This is related to the fact that Leon does not appear to have firm standards for which “customs” to ratify and which not. At any rate, one thing is clear: we are operating here in a realm of negotiation that is “down-to-earth,”
that exists between the emperor and his subjects and not between the emperor and God.

Still, the

So the good of the

Second, the citizens do not always wait for the legislator to tell them their interest. The polity is the abstracted concept of a community that is

On the whole Leon merely records the change, as if describing and governing a society comes to the same thing when one is an emperor.”

zh: 这种习惯与批准的动态，在中期所有法律工程中并不都同样主导、甚至并不都同样明显。约翰·哈尔登写道，在七世纪，“皇帝采取行动，所求的并非修订法律使之合于现实，而是改变现实，使其符合继承下来的法律和道德规范。”
哈尔登在这里处理的是
作为查士丁尼之后立法手段相对衰落的问题。然而，利奥六世是在一个既定的罗马法学传统内行动的，该传统承认习惯对立法者有一种要求权。正如吉尔·哈里斯就晚期古代所简洁表述的：
en: This dynamic of custom and ratification is not as dominant, or even evident, in all legal projects of the middle period. John Haldon has written about how, in the seventh century, “imperial action was not directed at emending laws to conform to reality, but rather at emending reality to conform to the inherited legal-moral apparatus.”
Haldon is addressing here the question of the relative decline of the

as a means of legislation after Justinian. Still, Leon VI was acting within an established tradition of Roman jurisprudence which recognized that custom had a claim on the lawgiver. As Jill Harries put it succinctly about late antiquity:

zh: 皇帝可以决定是否回应来自法律、社会和政治各方面的压力。这一权利事实上对皇帝自身作为立法者的合法性至关重要；他可以指望其敕令得到整个社会之同意——即
（全体一致）——的支持……皇帝们对社会变迁的开放，可能使其立法比原本可能的样子更能回应公共需要与变动中的社会风俗……从历史上看，罗马法始终包含一个道德维度，意味着它回应着当时的社会风俗，法学理论也承认，某些法律如何适用在很大程度上取决于社会态度。
en: Emperors were entitled to respond, or not, not only to legal pressures but to social and political pressures as well. This right was in fact essential to the emperor’s own legitimacy as a lawgiver; he could expect his constitutions to be backed by the consent of society as a whole, the

... The emperors’ openness to social change may have made their legislation more responsive to public needs and changing social mores than it would otherwise have been... Historically Roman law has always contained a moral dimension, meaning that it was responsive to the social mores of the time, and it was an accepted part of juristic theory that the application of some laws was heavily dependent on social attitudes.

zh: 下面这条法律意见被查士丁尼的
奉为圭臬，并保留在
（在利奥六世治下正式颁布的希腊语译本）中：“那些没有成文法的事项，应由习惯与惯例来治理……古老的习惯取代法律。所以正如法律被确立，无论它是成文的还是不成文的，它也同样被废止，或通过成文、或不通过成文，也就是通过弃用。”
正如我们所见，这是至少某些拜占庭皇帝所遵循的原则。利奥之子君士坦丁七世会用更强的措辞来表述“不成文习惯的在先效力”：ὅπερ ἡ συνήθεια ἀγράφως πρώην ἐκύρωσε（
在这里指正式权威或管辖权）。
十二世纪，历史学家兼法律学者约安尼斯·佐纳拉斯在其
中批评皇帝巴西尔二世，说他没有“按照盛行的习惯来统治，而立法权威已认为那些习惯适宜批准为法律；相反，他按照自己的意志来统治。”
en: The following legal opinion was enshrined in Justinian’s
and retained in the

(the Greek translation officially published under Leon VI): “Those matters about which there is no written law are to be governed by custom and usage... Ancient custom takes the place of law. So just as law is put in place, whether it is written or unwritten, so too is it annulled, either through writing or without it, that is, through lack of use.”

As we have seen, this was a principle followed by at least some Byzantine emperors. Leon’s son Konstantinos VII would use even stronger language for “the prior validity of unwritten custom”: ὅπερ ἡ συνήθεια ἀγράφως πρώην ἐκύρωσε (
here denotes official authority or jurisdiction).
In the twelfth century, the historian and legal scholar Ioannes Zonaras criticized in his
the emperor Basileios II for not ruling “according to the prevailing custom, which legislative authorities have deemed fit to ratify as law; instead, he ruled according to his own will.”

zh: 本书将就拜占庭政体力图捍卫的，正是与哈里斯为古代晚期描绘的图景相近的解释，既涉及法律，也涉及拜占庭政体本身是如何被理解的，以及它的政治领域。具体而言，政体被其统治者与臣民构想为一个建立在共享价值观之上的统一共同体，而政权的合法性，基于它在罗马“共和”传统中对其臣民之价值观与福祉的关切。这当然不是关于个人或群体在所有时候实际如何行为的陈述，而是关于支撑罗曼尼亚（Romanía）的意识形态、关于他们行动的道德与政治框架的陈述。这一框架在统治者与臣民之间创造了相互的责任，而皇帝在作决定之前必须为
把脉。法律本身也落入这个协商的场域。利奥把法律人格化，把它们当作隐喻性的臣属来对待，对其中一些他授予“官阶与头衔”（这里指法律效力），而另一些他则“放逐”（见序言），仿佛它们是官员。
因此，在对法律与人两者作决定时，皇帝们通过参与一场关于政体之性质与方向、关于什么将被纳入什么将被排除的持续的一般性讨论，来塑造
。法律（正如我们将在第三章更详细看到的）服从于关于共同善的盛行共识。我们不应以诉诸所谓的特殊利益集团来掩盖这一点。当利奥在某条
中提到“习惯”时，他通常指的是只在社会某一特定部分盛行的规范，即该
条款所适用的那部分（例如渔民）。但他并不那样框定它：他需要诉诸作为整体的“人民”，而非一个特殊利益集团，因为在罗马社会中改革正是这样被正当化的。倘若我们犬儒地把他的
拆解为游说集团，我们就会只见特殊利益的树木、不见意识形态的森林。
en: It is a picture such as the one that Harries paints for late antiquity that this book will seek to defend regarding the Byzantine polity, and not only about law but about its very conception and political sphere. Specifically, the polity was conceived by its rulers and subjects as a unified community founded on shared values, and the legitimacy of the regime was based on its solicitude for the values and welfare of its subjects in the Roman “republican” tradition. This is of course not a statement about how individuals or groups actually behaved at all times but rather about the ideology that underpinned Romanía, the moral and political framework of their actions. This framework created reciprocal responsibilities between rulers and subjects, and emperors had to take the pulse of the

before making decisions. The law itself fell into this arena of negotiation. Leon personified the laws and treated them as metaphorical subjects to some of whom he would bestow “ranks and titles” (here legal validity) while others he would “exile” (pref.), as if they were magistrates.
Therefore, in making decisions about both laws and persons, emperors were shaping the

by contributing to an ongoing general discussion about its nature and direction, about what would be included and what excluded. The law (as we will see in more detail in Chapter 3) was subject to the prevailing consensus about the common good. We should not obscure this point with reference to putative special-interest groups. When Leon refers to “customs” in a given
he is usually referring to norms prevailing only in a particular segment of society, the segment to which the provisions of that

apply (e.g., fishermen). But he does not frame it that way: he needed to invoke “the people” as a whole rather than a special-interest group, because that was how reforms were justified in Roman society. Were we to cynically disperse his
into lobbying groups, we would miss the ideological forest for the special-interest trees.

zh: 利奥

背后的道德逻辑与推理，包含通向这种意识形态的几把钥匙。虽然有些皇帝可能选择向政治共同体强加自己开出的条件，另一些皇帝，如利奥，则与政体进入了一种更具辩证性的关系。如果我们想理解皇帝采取行动时所依据的意识形态框架，也就是他明知自己置身其中的政治领域，我们就必须从后者那里获得指引。哈尔登论证说，“法律，无论其详细规定与要求是否被理解或适用，都象征着罗马国家……它作为国家之实践意识形态、以及人们赖以理解世界的那些政治—文化信念的理论背景而存在。”
臣民与统治者构想其相互关系所依据的条款，就编码在那里，我们必须密切留意它们。然而，至今还没有关于拜占庭
概念、或关于它所指向的那个领域的研究。鉴于它对所有拜占庭人——皇帝与臣民皆然——的政治思维的核心地位，我们现在必须问：利奥不断提及的这个
究竟是什么？
en: The moral logic and reasoning behind Leon’s

contain several keys to this ideology. While some emperors may have chosen to dictate their terms to the polity, others, such as Leon, entered into a more dialectical relationship with it. It is from the latter that we must take the lead if we wish to understand the ideological framework of imperial action, the political sphere in which it self-consciously operated. Haldon argues that “the law, whether or not its detailed prescriptions and demands were understood or applied, symbolized the Roman state... It existed as the theoretical backdrop to the practical ideology of the state and to the political-cultural beliefs upon which people based their understanding of the world.”
The terms on which subjects and rulers conceived their mutual relationship are encoded there, and we must attend to them closely. However, there has yet been no study of the Byzantine notion of the
or of the sphere to which it points. Given its centrality to the political thinking of all Byzantines, emperors and subjects alike, we must now ask, what was this
to which Leon keeps referring?

zh: 拜占庭的政体概念
en: The Byzantine Concept of the Politeia

zh: 显然，像通常所做的那样把
译为“国家”（state）并不令人满意。
利奥对该词及其同源词的大多数用法，若按这种受限的意义来理解都会说不通（我们将在下面考察现代“国家”概念及其问题）。利奥提到
时，心里想的当然是整个罗马社会，但同时他并不想把它理论化为独立于国家机构与他自己的法律之外：他没有一种由与国家分离的私人利益所构成的“市民社会”概念。
他相信一个恰当的
没有良法就无法存在，但同时又勉强承认其某些要素在法律认可之前、或未经法律认可就在运作。在我们追溯这个术语的谱系之前，让我们先通过考察不同体裁的文本来弄清它在这一时期具有哪些含义。
en: Clearly, it is not satisfactory to translate
as “state,” as is commonly done.

Most of Leon’s uses of the word and its cognates would not make sense if taken in this restrictive sense (we will examine modern notions of “the state” and their problems below). Leon certainly has the whole of Roman society in mind when he refers to the

but at the same time he does not want to theorize it as independent of the institutions of the state and his own laws: he has no notion of a “civil society” constituted by private interests that are separate from the state.
He believes that a proper

cannot exist without good laws but at the same time reluctantly grants that some of its elements are operating prior to or without receiving legal sanction. Before we trace the genealogy of this term, let us flesh out its semantic range in this period by examining texts in different genres.

zh: 大概是在九世纪，某位叙利亚诺斯（Syrianos）写了一部军事手册，后来利奥六世在该世纪末撰写自己的
（Taktika）时把它用作来源。
为了框定军事科学的社会语境，叙利亚诺斯在其论著的第一章列举了
的各个部分，尽管其著作的开头至少失去了一页。文本开篇处我们看到“语法与修辞教师、医生、农民，以及从事类似职业者”。他补充了祭司、律师、多种商人与工匠，以及“非生产性阶层”，如体弱者、老人与儿童，“他们无法为共同体的需要（τὴν τῶν κοινῶν χρείαν）贡献任何东西”。他说，所有这些都“是
的各个部分”。他考虑过加入有闲阶层，但决定不加，因为他们毫无贡献（而且大概，与体弱者、老人和儿童不同，他们没有借口）。他通过活体的有机隐喻来想象政体：“正如在人体中你找不到任何没有功能的单一部件，同样在最好的
中也不应有任何部件，在能够为
的福祉作贡献时却无所作为。”在第二章，他列举了
每一部分的功能，而在第三章他解释了主持每一部分的那些人的道德与专业资质：他们几乎全都是某种国家官员。再一次，政体被想象为在共同福祉这一理想下看待的整个社会，而非独立于国家机构之外。我们所谓的“国家”是政体中一个完全整合的部分，但又是与其他部分不同的部分，因为它以官方身份行事：它着眼于共同善来规制各个要素，从而使政体的运作在其成员看来具有正当性。
en: It was probably in the ninth century that a certain Syrianos wrote a military manual later used as a source by Leon VI when he wrote his own
at the end of the century.
To frame the social context of military science, Syrianos, in the first chapter of his treatise, lists the parts of the

though the first page or more of his work has been lost. When the text begins we find “teachers of grammar and rhetoric, physicians, farmers, and those in like professions.” He adds priests, lawyers, many types of merchants and craftsmen, and “the unproductive classes,” such as the infirm, the old, and children, “who are unable to contribute anything to the needs of the community (τὴν τῶν κοινῶν χρείαν).” All these, he says, “are the parts of the

” He considers adding the leisured classes but decides not to because they contribute nothing (and presumably, unlike the infirm, the old, and children, they have no excuse). He imagines the polity through the organic metaphor of the living body: “Just as in the human body you will not find any single part that has no function, so too in the best
there should be no part that, while it is able to contribute to the welfare of the
does nothing.” In the second chapter, he lists the functions of each part of the

while in the third he explains the moral and professional qualifications of those men who preside over each part: almost all of them are state officials of one kind or another. Again, the polity is imagined as the whole of society under the ideal aspect of the common good, and not independently of the institutions of the state. What we call “the state” is a fully integrated part of the polity, but a part different from the others in that it acts in an official capacity: it regulates the various elements with an eye on the common good and thereby makes the operations of the polity legitimate in its own eyes.

zh: 叙利亚诺斯的
不能译为“国家”。译者乔治·丹尼斯在这里、且仅在这里把它译为“公民的各个阶层”。但在翻译标题时，他却用“治国术”和“国家”，尽管是同一个词。叙利亚诺斯心里想的是我们所谓“社会”在其全部多样性中的整体。当他在引介军事科学时回顾它，他称之为“参与
的众多平民”。
我们在这里也可以用“民众”或“无武装的公民”。然而同时，他把这个社会视为一个与政府机构紧密相连并受其规制的有机整体。这也是利奥想象人民与法律之关系的方式：法律是隐喻性的官员。这个有机体有一种共同善，叙利亚诺斯称之为τὰ κοινά，而他根据各个肢体对那种共同善的贡献来评价它们。正如我们将看到的，τὰ κοινά只是透过

集体利益之棱镜来指称它的一种方式。利奥六世曾想象其立法以同样的方式运作：“那些愿意通过自己的努力设计出某种供生活使用的益处的人，把它做成供所有人共享（ἐν κοινῷ）的益处，这是高贵而恰当的；这比想要把它限于一个小群体、并把所有其他人排除在外要好。由法律所带来的恩惠应当是公共的（κοινήν），这就更加恰当了。正如领导者的德性一样，法律也是如此：我们有责任使来自它的好处在所有统治者与被统治者之间被共同（κοινῇ）享有。”
这一原则强烈地申明了共同善相对于个人利益的优越性。
en: Syrianos’s

cannot be translated as “the state.” The translator George Dennis here and only here translates it as “the various classes of citizens.” But when translating the headings, he goes with “statecraft” and “the state,” though it is the same word. Syrianos has in mind the whole of what we call “society” in all its diversity. When he looks back at it in introducing the military science, he calls it “the multitude of civilians who take part in the

We could also go with “populace” here or “unarmed citizens.” At the same time, however, he takes this society to be an organic whole integrally linked with and regulated by government institutions. This is also how Leon imagined the relation between the people and the laws: the laws are metaphorical magistrates. This organism has a common good, which Syrianos calls τὰ κοινά, and he evaluates its various limbs based on what they contribute to that common good. As we will see, τὰ κοινά was only a way of designating the

through the prism of its collective interests. Leon VI had imagined his legislation working in the same way: “It is nobly fitting for those who are willing to devise, through their own efforts, some benefit for use in life, to make it a benefit for all in common (ἐν κοινῷ); this is better than to want to limit it to a small group, and exclude all others from it. It is all the more fitting that the benefaction caused by the laws should be common (κοινήν). Just as with the virtue of a leader, so too with the laws: it is our duty that the good that comes from it should be enjoyed in common (κοινῇ) by all rulers and ruled alike.”
This principle strongly affirms the superiority of the common good over individual interests.

zh: 换言之，尽管叙利亚诺斯对其社会持一种全局观并分类其组成部分，他却并不对它持一种纯描述性的看法。“最好的
”这一规范性概念，是他关于

应当努力成为一个好的政体。这是他那思路的全局延伸：
的每一个特定部分，无论是医生、律师还是官员，也都应当努力成为
医生、律师和官员。
他提供了一种在国家监护之下的统一社会的有机愿景，在其中任何一方离开另一方都无法存在。很难用现代术语来表述这一点，因为它基于一种统一的共同善观念，而非对分离利益的平衡。与利奥一样，叙利亚诺斯并不把
的诸要素视为构成一个自立的私人利益世界（一个“市民社会”），而“国家”作为一个规制机构被强加于其上。我们所谓的国家被内建于这个共同体的肌理与根本目的之中，因为这个共同体由其共同善所界定，而“国家”正是使它能够实现共同善的东西。
en: In other words, for all that Syrianos takes a global view of his society and classifies its constituent parts, he does not have a purely descriptive view of it. The normative concept of “the best
” is part and parcel of his very concept of a
in other words, he believes that a proper
ought to try to be a good one. This is a global extension of his thinking that each particular part of the
whether doctors, lawyers, or magistrates, also ought to strive to be
doctors, lawyers, and magistrates.

He offers an organic vision of a unified society under the tutelage of the state, in which neither side can exist without the other. It is hard to put this in modern terms because it is based on a unified idea of the common good and not on a balancing of separate interests. As with Leon, Syrianos does not view the elements of the

as constituting a self-standing world of private interests (a “civil society”) over which “the state” is imposed as a regulatory agency. What we call the state is built into the fabric and the very purpose of this collective because the collective is defined by its common good and “the state” is what enables it to achieve it.

zh: 叙利亚诺斯对政体各部分的分类，在法律或其他意义上都不是官方的。任何观察拜占庭社会的作家都可以作出一种不同的分类，通常是适合他当下目标的那种。然而他们确实共享的，是一个统一共和国之共同善的概念。在宫廷诗人科里普斯归于查士丁二世（565年）的那篇长篇即位演说中，他把
（罗马统治权）比作一个单一的身体，只是他真正谈论的是
，如果我们用“帝国”指各行省，这就不是在说“帝国”；事实上他在演说中段就称之为
。它的头是皇帝，元老们是胸与臂，下层等级是脚（他特别挑出农民加以关注），而国库是胃。
一部农学论著

分为三个部分：军队、神职人员和农事”。
这是“所有人”的简略说法。十一世纪晚期的历史学家阿塔莱亚特斯承认，工匠与劳工（βάναυσοι）也为
贡献有用的东西。
每一个想吸引皇帝注意、或为自己的领域或职业争取益处的人，都会把它做成
的关键划分之一，恰恰是为了论证它对共同善不可或缺。例如，利奥六世在其
序言中说，军事科学是“
事务”的一个本质要素，他在同一句中把这个短语与“罗马人的事务”同义使用。
举一个相关的例子，959年为
（寝宫总管）巴西尔撰写的一部海战论著，其序言开篇就宣称，海战“对生活之有用、并构成一个

诚然是夸张，但在拜占庭，任何东西的重要性正是这样衡量的：它对政体贡献了什么？君士坦丁七世本人被其传记作者赞扬为“以智慧装饰并丰富了罗马人的

因此，共同善总是相对于政体来界定的，它涵盖并规范一切具有社会或道德价值的活动，无论是否由国家组织。
en: Syrianos’s classification of the parts of the polity was not official in a legal or other sense. Any writer looking at Byzantine society could produce a different classification, usually one that suited his objectives at that moment. What they do share, however, is a concept of the common good of a unified republic. In the long accession-speech attributed to him by the court poet Corippus, Justin II (in 565) compares the
to a single body, only he is really talking about the
not the “empire” if by that we mean the provinces, and in fact he calls it the

in the middle of the speech. Its head is the emperor, the senators are the breast and arms, the lower orders are the feet (he singles out the farmers for special attention), and the treasury is the stomach.
The preface to a treatise on agriculture
dedicated in the mid-tenth century to Leon’s son, Konstantinos VII, states that the emperor knows that “the
is divided into three parts: the military, the priesthood, and agriculture.”
This is shorthand for “everyone.” The historian Attaleiates in the late eleventh century conceded that craftsmen and workmen (βάναυσοι) also contributed useful things to the
Everyone who wanted to attract imperial attention or claim a benefit for his own field or profession would make it one of the key divisions of the
precisely in order to argue that it was indispensable for the common good. For example, in the preface of his
Leon VI states that military science was an essential element of the “affairs of the
” a phrase that he uses synonymously in the same sentence with “the affairs of the Romans.”
To give a related example, the preface to a treatise on naval warfare composed in 959 for the
Basileios begins by declaring that naval warfare is “as useful for life and constitutes a
” as nothing else.

Hyperbole, to be sure, but that was how the importance of anything was gauged in Byzantium: what did it contribute to the polity? Konstantinos VII was himself praised by his biographer for “adorning and enriching the
of the Romans with wisdom,” given that “there are many noble and praiseworthy sciences, technical arts, and disciplines in our
The common good, therefore, was defined always in relation to the polity, and it embraced and governed both state and nonstate activities—all of them that had any social or moral value.

zh: 我们应当以这种精神来理解

由成员与肢体构成，方式与人相似，而最大、最必要的部分是皇帝与牧首。”
这些分类体系没有一个是穷尽的或排他的，因为每一个都只旨在提升作者当下直接关心的那个政体要素（就这部文本而言，是牧首职）。它们揭示，政体是一个集体，每一类职业或每一个人——包括皇帝——都是按其对这个共同体福祉所起的作用来界定的。事实上，把皇帝视为政体的一部分几乎没有什么争议，尽管
试图设定他与牧首之间的平等、并区分他们的管辖权，这却是有争议的。
en: It is in this spirit that we should take the opening lines of the

is constituted of members and limbs, in a like manner to human beings, and the greatest and most necessary parts are the emperor and the patriarch.”

None of these classificatory systems was either exhaustive or exclusive, as each was designed to promote only the element of the polity that was of immediate concern to the author at that moment (in the case of this text, the patriarchate). They reveal that the polity was a collectivity in terms of whose good every type of profession or person was defined, including the emperor. In fact, treating the emperor as part of the polity was hardly controversial, though the
’s attempt to postulate an equality between him and the patriarch and to distinguish their jurisdiction was.

但在经由
从
转向“国家”的过程中，某种东西丢失了，即一种社会的全局观，被一种更窄的视野——即“行政”的视野——所取代。普塞洛斯的视角之所以这样收窄，与所用的颂辞体裁有关。我们在处理帝国演说的证据时应当记住这一点：为了把聚光灯——如它们必须做的那样——打在一个人身上，它们把其它一切贬置到边缘，或专门从皇帝的观点来看待它。于是，就有可能从
或

en: The modern study of Byzantine politics and political ideology has largely effaced the concept of the

Translating

In practice, of course, the
and

Therefore, some (not all) of Syrianos’s parts of the polity, for example, soldiers, tax-inspectors, and judges, could also be seen as aspects of imperial administration. According to Psellos, when Konstantinos IX ascended the throne, he saw that the

was a “composite thing” and had to appoint generals to govern one part of it, judges to another, advisors to a third, and so on. “And lest the state (τὸ κράτος) be broken into its parts,” he appointed one man to oversee it all, the honorand of the speech, Konstantinos Leichoudes.
But in moving from the

something has been lost, namely, a global view of society, replaced with a more narrow view, namely, that of “administration.” This narrowing was a function of Psellos’s genre, panegyric. We should remember this when dealing with the evidence of imperial orations: to shine the spotlight, as they must, on one person, they relegate everything else to the sidelines or see it exclusively from the imperial point of view. Thus it was possible to view the

在这里他交替使用这些术语：κράτος（“国家”）、τὸ πολιτικὸν σῶμα（“政治体”或“民政”）、τὰ πολιτικὰ πράγματα（“政治事务”）、以及τὸ σῶμα τῆς πολιτείας（“

en: Let us stay with Psellos for a moment. His orations and

Here he uses the terms κράτος (“the state”), τὸ πολιτικὸν σῶμα (“the body politic” or “the civil administration”), τὰ πολιτικὰ πράγματα (“political affairs”), and τὸ σῶμα τῆς πολιτείας (“the body of the

In a later section, he compares the

This was a narrower conception of the

The answer is: from ancient Rome, whose direct descendent Byzantium was in an unbroken line of political and ideological continuity. The Byzantine

en: Calling Byzantium (or any Roman-style empire) a “republic” will strike most readers as counterintuitive. In modern times, increasingly since the eighteenth century, monarchies and republics have been viewed as mutually exclusive types of regimes. This has been reinforced by the modern (not Roman) convention of using the labels “Republic” and “Empire” to distinguish two phases of Roman history. But
in Roman usage (

in Byzantine Greek translation) did not refer to the type of regime that governed the polity. It referred rather to certain underlying aspects of a polity that, among other things, legitimated the use of state power in a context of popular sovereignty. In the eyes of the Romans themselves, what we call “the Empire” was just another phase of the history of the Roman

for the purpose of state power and the theory of popular sovereignty did not necessarily change in the transition from the regime of the consuls to that of the emperors. This section will try to look past the distracting conventions of modern terminology to unearth Roman and Byzantine notions about the continuity of the

For example, it could refer to the regimen or “lifestyle” of a person or group, such as monks, a usage we find in hagiography. It could refer to a city, though this was uncommon.
In classical authors, however, it referred primarily to the type of regime by which a city-state was governed, especially the arrangement of its offices. There were various types of
for example monarchy, aristocracy, and democracy.
Many of these senses survived in Byzantium. But here we will focus on its dominant meaning in Byzantine political, legal, and historical texts, where

We encounter a range of additional terms for that concept in the sources, which correspond to different senses of the Latin original (

我们将回到这一定义的意涵，但首先有必要作一些术语上的观察。

en: In ancient Rome,

Harriet Flower’s definition, based on ancient Roman sources, elucidates the concept that we explicated based on the texts of Syrianos, Leon VI, and others: “the term

suggests the unity of all citizens in a shared civic community that transcends the social divisions of class, neighborhood, or family. Such a community is fundamentally at odds with the whole concept of political parties that divide citizens into permanent factions or allegiance groups.”
The

We will come back to the implications of this definition, but some terminological observations are first in order.

zh: 西塞罗认为，国君、贵族或人民都有可能治理好一个

西塞罗对王政时期罗马的看法表明，他承认一个君主制

而他笔下的西庇阿，在被逼迫从三种简单宪制形式（而非罗马的混合宪制）中选择其一时，选择了君主制。所以西塞罗并不把君主制视为与
不相容，尽管他确实认为它带来僭主制与丧失法治的风险。
反过来，西塞罗对元老院（他自己偏好的领导治理机构）在

所以按西塞罗的看法，

詹姆斯·汉金斯最近揭示了文艺复兴时期的那些辩论，它们逐渐导致
这个术语被专门与非君主制政体联系起来。
这是近代政治演变的结果。然而直到那一刻，该术语或多或少保留了其原初的罗马含义，而那种含义并不特定于某种政体。
en: Cicero allowed for the possibility of a

governed well by kings, an aristocracy, or a democracy: “provided the bond holds firm, which in the first place fastened the people to each other in the fellowship of a community, any of these three types may be, not indeed perfect, nor in my view the best, but at least tolerable.”
Cicero’s view of Rome under the kings shows that he recognized the possibility of a monarchical
and his Scipio, when pressed to choose one of three simple constitutional forms (rather than the mixed constitution of Rome), opts for monarchy. So Cicero did not view monarchy as incompatible with a
although he did think that it posed the risk of tyranny and loss of the rule of law.
Conversely, Cicero’s exaggerated view of the role and power in the
of the senate (his own preferred leading body of governance) could have easily been said by a Byzantine thinker about his emperor.
So according to Cicero the

was not regime-specific: monarchies could be republican. This understanding of “republican” survived until early modern times. Some early modern theorists also maintained that republican monarchies were viable.
James Hankins has recently exposed the debates of the Renaissance that gradually led to the term
being associated exclusively with nonmonarchical regimes.
This was a function of modern politics. Down to that point, however, the term had more or less retained its original Roman meaning, which was not regime-specific.

zh: 此外，斯科菲尔德已表明，西塞罗对
的讨论主要不是关于最优政体类型，而是关于政府（无论它采取何种形式）之
的根据，而且他的论证依赖于鲜明的罗马概念，这些概念在希腊传统中几乎没有先例；毕竟，这正是西塞罗呈现其自身计划的方式。
在希腊理论中，最优类型的
被塑造为一种德性的政体，较少是法律的政体，而它的正当性根本无涉民众的共识。虽然关于拜占庭人民主权的论证将在本书后面两章中作出，但我在这里提出的论点是：罗马的
观念支撑着拜占庭的
：它事实上就是同一个“罗马人的
”，只是处于其历史的较后阶段。正如一部六世纪论著（如今用希腊语）呼应西塞罗所说，“一个
是一个由许多人构成的
[共享之物]。”
从四世纪开始（也可能早在三世纪），拜占庭人已给这个共和国起了一个名字：罗曼尼亚（Romanía）。那么，我们可以把拜占庭的政体称为一个“帝国共和国”，
也就是一个有皇帝的共和国（与一个扩张主义共和国相对）。更可取的是，我们应当称它为共和式君主制、君主制共和国，或干脆叫“处于其君主阶段的罗马共和国”。
若干学者已提出这样的术语，尽管有时带着通常那种任意的限制（“直到戴克里先统治为止”）。
en: Moreover, Schofield has shown that Cicero’s discussion of the

In Greek theory, the best type of

was cast as a regime of virtue, less so of law, and there was no question of its legitimacy being grounded in popular consensus. While the argument for popular sovereignty in Byzantium will be made in two later chapters of this book, the case I am making here is that the Roman idea of the

of the Romans” in a later phase of its history. As a sixth-century treatise echoed Cicero (now in Greek), “a
is a

Starting in the fourth century (and possibly in the third), the Byzantines had given this republic a name: Romanía. We could, then, call the regime of Byzantium an “imperial republic,”

that is, a republic with an emperor (as opposed to an expansionist republic). Preferably, we should call it a republican monarchy, monarchical republic, or just “the Roman Republic in its monarchic phase.”
A number of scholars have proposed such terms, though sometimes with the usual arbitrary limitations (“until the reign of Diocletian”).

zh: 但现代在“共和国”（the Republic）与“帝国”（the Empire）之间的区分又怎么说呢？这一区分可能仍使把拜占庭称为共和国显得反直觉。然而它在很大程度上是现代的，并妨碍我们理解原初术语。“共和国”（Republic）是一个现代误称。要看到这一点，我们必须区分：罗马人（无论在奥古斯都之前还是之后）如何使用
这个术语，与我们的学术如何把它征用为一个（政治化且道德说教的）标签、用来指罗马史的一个时期。实际上，对我们来说，它与其说是一个时期的标签（像“古典”与“古风”那样），不如说是某种特定政体类型——即由执政官治理的那种——的标签。然而罗马人与拜占庭人双方都能够、而且确实区分了
与
被治理的方式（见下文）。用“共和国”（republic）这个术语来指一个时期和一种政体形式（执政官或元老院的政体），是
语言的一个特征。再引弗劳尔的话：“罗马人自己并没有一种用专门指称共和国的术语来给其政府贴标签的方式……此外，
仍是随后那个‘帝国’时期用来描述政府的术语，无论皇帝还是他们的批评者都如此使用。”
我们所谓的“共和国”，对他们而言不过是
漫长历史中的一种治理政体。治理形式可以改变，作为基础的
则始终存在。于是，我们可以作出一个区分：“共和的”（republican）指向
的原初含义，而“共和国的”（Republican）指罗马史某一阶段的时期与制度。
en: But what about the modern distinction between “the Republic” and “the Empire”? This distinction may still make it counterintuitive to call Byzantium a republic. It is, however, largely modern and interferes with our understanding of the original terms. The “Republic” is a modern misnomer. To see this we have to make a distinction between how the Romans, both before and after Augustus, used the term

and how our scholarship has pressed it into service as a (politicized and moralizing) label for a period of Roman history. Actually, with us it is not so much a label for a period (in the way that Classical and Archaic are) as it is for a particular type of regime, that governed by the consuls. Both Romans and Byzantines alike, however, could and did distinguish between the
and the way in which the
was governed (see below). Use of the term “republic” to refer to a period and a form of regime (that of the consuls or the senate) is a feature of the
languages. To quote Flower again: “The Romans themselves did not have a way of labeling their government with terms that specifically designated a republic... Moreover,
was the term still employed to describe the government during the subsequent ‘imperial’ period, both by emperors and by their critics.”
What we call “the Republic” was for them but one regime of governance in the long history of the
The
itself was what underlay regime-change. Thus, we can draw a distinction between “republican,” which points to the original meanings of
and “Republican,” which refers to the period and institutions of one phase of Roman history.

changed from that of the consuls to that of emperors. (Witness, for example, Arcadius Charisius, a jurist of the Tetrarchy:

children: regimentis rei publicae ad imperatores perpetuos translatis.

他有争议地声称自己恢复了
而同时代人会以或多或少的怀疑来回应这一声称，取决于他们认为某种特定政体类型对

en: To be sure, dramatic changes occurred in the transition from the consuls to the monarchy, but this was not taken by the vast majority of Romans to mean that their

He controversially claimed to have restored the
and contemporaries would have greeted this claim with more or less skepticism depending on how integral they believed a specific type of regime was to the essence of the
Few were as skeptical as the mainstream of modern scholarship has been.

我们将在下面讨论这一观念如何在希腊语中、在拜占庭人可获得的文本中被理论化。
en: The
in ancient Rome and the

His tone is melodramatic and his purpose is ironic, to remind readers that it is part of the definition of a true

But his was a partial and even personal view. He knew that the

We will discuss below how this notion was theorized in Greek, in texts available to the Byzantines.

观念。我们那种党派性术语的问题在于：它要求我们在少数史料只是反映君主制下对

但

的需要与利益，这在当时与之后都被承认。塔西佗明确指出，各行省更喜欢皇帝而非元老院，因为他们不信任元老院。
在历史学家维莱伊乌斯（在提比略治下写作）那里，“罗马不是从共和国走向元首制，而是从共和国走向一个更好的共和国。”
在欧特罗皮乌斯——一位概览共和国与帝国两者的四世纪历史学家——那里，
压倒性地被用于帝国，比例几乎达二十比一。欧特罗皮乌斯赞扬奥古斯都带来和平、让罗马繁荣。语言是说明性的：拉丁语作

至少有一部现代教科书同意：“道德说教者或许会继续大谈‘美好的旧时光’，但按大多数清醒的历史衡量标准，罗马最好的日子其实正要开始。”
en: For Tacitus, the old

was in some respects better than the new one because in it men such as himself were “free,” though it is doubtful that it was better for anyone else. Modern scholarship has made his idiosyncratic view of the

the foundation for its periodization and theorization of Roman history. This theorization has contributed decisively to the negative view of Byzantium that has prevailed for so long. Therefore, what I am advocating is that we listen to our other sources for a change—the vast majority of them, in fact—and consider the less politically partisan notion of a
held by most Romans of the empire, including the Byzantines. The problem with our partisan terminology is that it requires us to talk about the
where a handful of sources are only reflecting nostalgia under the monarchy for
ἐλευθερία),

and to forget that they have a narrow conception of what freedom entailed. We tend to blur the distinction between “senatorial” interests and “republican ideology” and thereby conclude that the latter was essentially antimonarchical.
But the
was not just about the senate. In many respects, the monarchy served the needs and interests of the
better than the late Republic, as was recognized at the time and afterward. Tacitus is explicit that the provinces preferred the emperor over the senate, which they mistrusted.
In the historian Velleius (writing under Tiberius), “Rome has not moved from Republic to Principate, but from Republic to a better Republic.”
In Eutropius, a fourth-century historian surveying both the Republic and the empire,
is used overwhelmingly for the empire, by a factor of almost twenty to one. Eutropius praised Augustus for bringing about peace and allowing Rome to flourish. The language is indicative:
in the Latin, ἤνθησε γοῦν τὰ τῆς Ῥώμης πράγματα in the Greek translation.
At least one modern textbook concurs: “Moralists might continue to hold forth about the ‘good old days,’ but by most sober historical measures, Rome’s best days actually were just about to begin.”

zh: 学术中的“共和国”（Republican）偏见，就是假定奥古斯都之后没有
。这实际上只是我们这一方的术语混淆。我们不应把少数人对“自由”（实际上是他们自己的特权地位）的怀旧，当作界定什么是、什么不是
的标准。西塞罗很可能会同意塔西佗的评估，即我们所谓的元首制不是一个“真正的”
，但那个裁决在很大程度上会是过渡得以完成的那种暴力方式、以及他个人对它的经验的结果。西塞罗自己哀叹
在内战
就已经丧失，但他这样说的意思是有德性领袖的出现减少了。

en: The “Republican” bias in scholarship is the assumption that there was no

after Augustus. This is actually only a terminological confusion on our part. We should not take a few men’s nostalgia for “freedom” (in reality, their own privileged position) as a standard for defining what is and what is not a
Cicero would probably have agreed with Tacitus’s assessment that what we call the Principate was not a “true”
but that verdict would largely have been a result of the violent way in which the transition was accomplished and his personal experience of it. Cicero himself lamented that the
had already been lost
the civil wars, but he meant by this a decline in the emergence of virtuous leaders.
This is another personal view that should also not be (and has not been) made the basis for modern periodization.

zh: 当学者们断言“罗马即便在君主制下也仍是一个
，即便不在事实上、至少在名义上”时，
他们是在作一个基于罗马史之道德—政治看法的区分。他们实际上是在站在早期元首制下少数元老一边，那些元老渴望他们失去的“自由”。但为什么他们的观点应当是决定性的？绝大多数其他罗马人，包括拜占庭人，认为他们也有一个
，只要：(a) 其政府的合法性最终基于它对人民负责，人民是其真正的基础（西塞罗的
）；(b) 其社会基于法律（他的
）；(c) 他们不是人群的随机聚合，而是一个有共同价值观的民族（他的
）。本书将论证拜占庭是一个共和式君主制，但不是基于共和制度的存续、不是基于权力行使中人身关系与非人身关系的平衡、也不是基于政体的“风格”——这些有时是那些在帝国之下寻找共和国痕迹的学者所遵循的方法论线索。
它将关乎界定并支撑政治领域的那个政体的意识形态，而我们对利奥六世
的初步考察表明，这一搜寻不会徒劳。它也将关乎共和国各要素在政治领域中的行为，这将揭示这种意识形态也见于实际政治，超出了抽象概念的层面。拜占庭在实践中也是一个罗马共和国。
en: When scholars assert that “Rome remained a
even under the monarchy in name if not in fact,”

they are making a distinction that is based on a moral-political view of Roman history. They are effectively taking the side of a minority of senators under the early Principate who pined for their lost “liberty.” But why should their outlook be decisive? The vast majority of other Romans, including the Byzantines, held that they too had a
insofar as (a) the legitimacy of their government was ultimately based in its accountability to the people, who were its true foundation (Cicero’s
); (b) their society was based on law (his
); and (c) they were not a random aggregate of peoples but a nation with common values (his

). This book will argue for a republican monarchy in Byzantium but not based on the survival of Republican institutions, on the balance of personal and impersonal relations in the exercise of power, or on the “style” of the regime, which have, at times, been the methodological cues followed by scholars who look for traces of the Republic under the empire.
It will be about the ideology of the polity that defined and sustained the political sphere, and our preliminary look at the

of Leon VI suggests that the search will not be fruitless. It will also be about the behavior of the elements of the republic in the political sphere, which will reveal that this ideology was not limited to a rarefied conceptual level. Byzantium was a Roman republic in practice too.

zh: 我随即会转向古代与拜占庭史料，它们表明
被认为在从共和国向帝国的过渡中存续了下来：统治形式经历更替，
仍是其基础。但首先，作为对前面讨论的收尾，值得指出我们的罗马史分期何等成问题。史学知识按一套套术语划分领域，割裂并遮蔽了共和国的连续性：共和国与帝国之间有一道划分，然后帝国又被拆分为元首制、多米那特制与拜占庭。弗劳尔警告说，虽然“分期构成历史语境中任何解释与评论的基础，但它绝不应被简单地视为理所当然，而应作为历史分析的基础被定期重新评估。”
这个基础的一个问题是，它仍深深浸透着过时的道德说教观念。这严重影响了拜占庭研究，而拜占庭传统上被认为在一个衰落叙事中占据最后且最低的位置。那个叙事基本上编码了一个“自由”递减的元叙事，从共和国到元首制、再到拜占庭，而启蒙史学认为拜占庭在政治与宗教两个领域都极度不自由。例如，吉本就把罗马与拜占庭的长期故事写成一个自由衰落的故事，而僭主制显然被东正教强化了。
正是这个令人反感的元叙事，加上对史料的无知，使得罗马史较早时期的优秀历史学家能够断然声称，在拜占庭“一切共和主义的伪装都已消失……没有人把皇帝视为专制君主以外的任何东西……这些意识形态主张合法的统治者是由神启示、由神拣选的。”
我们将会看到，这是相当误导的。
en: I will presently turn to ancient and Byzantine sources that demonstrate that the
was held to have survived the transition from Republic to empire: the

underlay regime-change. But first it is worth pointing out, by way of concluding the previous discussion, how problematic our periodization of Roman history is. The continuity of the republic is broken up and obscured by the compartmentalization of knowledge into semantic fields: there is a division between Republic and Empire, and then the Empire is broken up into Principate, Dominate, and Byzantium. Flower has warned that while “periodization forms the basis of any interpretation and commentary in a historical context, it should never be simply taken for granted, but should be regularly re-evaluated as the foundation of historical analysis.”

One problem with this foundation is that it remains deeply imbued with outdated moralizing notions. This has seriously affected the study of Byzantium, which has traditionally been held to occupy the final and lowest place in a narrative of decline. That narrative basically encodes a metanarrative of diminishing “freedom,” from Republic to Principate and then on to Byzantium, which Enlightenment historiography believed was supremely unfree in both the political and religious spheres. Gibbon, for example, had made the long-term story of Rome and Byzantium one of declining liberty, and tyranny was apparently strengthened by Orthodoxy.

It is this invidious metanarrative, reinforced by an ignorance of the sources, that enables good historians of earlier periods of Roman history to assert roundly that in Byzantium “all pretense of republicanism had vanished... no one thought of the emperor as anything other than an autocratic monarch... these ideologies argued that legitimate rulers were divinely inspired and divinely chosen.”
This, we will see, is quite misleading.

zh: 这个元叙事最奇怪的方面之一，是人们发明名称以赋予其四个时期以实在性的方式。“共和国”是在近代有些政治思想家判定共和国与君主制不相容时被发明的。“元首制”——来自拉丁词
，奥古斯都自称的许多东西之一——反映皇帝的至高地位，而“多米那特制”则基于后来皇帝使用的
（主人）一词，这个词显然为……元首制时期那些更爱自由的罗马人所憎恶。但没有罗马人用这些标签来指罗马史的时期或政体类型。实际上，从元首制到多米那特制的漫长过渡，涉及一个更大官僚机构的创建与文化变迁的加剧。这些趋势在元首制时期就已可见，并不包含任何本质性的断裂。头衔与宫廷意象的变化，并不能证明罗马史在那时终结的结论。如今人们普遍怀疑那次过渡中有多大变化。
至于“拜占庭”，它是一个基于
名称的现代术语，用来指称实际上是罗马国家历史中一个较后阶段的东西，它作为一个术语的功能，始终是把它标记为与其前身“本质上”不同。单就自由这个标准而言，从多米那特制到拜占庭的过渡，并无证据表明后者更不“自由”。但在长期衰落的道德剧中，拜占庭代表基督教神权政治与东方专制主义（这些术语仍在使用）；
按这种说法，拜占庭充满奴性、希腊习气与迷信，左右它的是宦官和宫廷阴谋，而且疆域也更小。正是基于这样的道德说教观念、虚假与不相干的标准，时期被划分、“本质”被界定，而学术专业化又阻止了那些本应揭露这个叙事真面目的交流。
en: One of the most curious aspects of this metanarrative is the way in which names have been invented to give reality to its four periods. The “Republic” was invented when segments of modern political thought decided that republics and monarchies were incompatible. The “Principate”—from Latin
one of the many things that Augustus called himself—reflects the emperor’s supremacy, while “Dominate” is based on the word

used by later emperors, a word that was apparently anathema to the more freedom-loving Romans of... the Principate. But no Roman used these labels to refer to periods of Roman history or to types of regimes. In reality, the long transition from the Principate to the Dominate involved the creation of a larger bureaucracy and an intensification of cultural changes. These trends were visible already in the Principate and entailed no essential rupture. Changes of titulature and court imagery do not justify the conclusion that Roman history ended at that time. It is common now to doubt that much changed in that transition.
As for “Byzantium,” which is a modern term based on a

name used to designate what was in reality a later phase in the history of the Roman state, its function as a term has always been to mark it off as “essentially” different from its predecessor. To question only one criterion, there is nothing in the transition from Dominate to Byzantium that suggests the latter was less “free.” But in the morality play of the long decline, Byzantium stands for Christian theocracy and oriental despotism (terms that are still used);

it was servile, Greekish, and superstitious; it was governed by eunuchs and palace intrigue; and it was smaller in size. It is precisely on the basis of such moralizing notions, falsehoods, and irrelevant criteria that periods have been divided and “essences” defined, while academic specialization has prevented exchanges that should have exposed this narrative for what it is.

zh: 这些标签与分期能否基于史料与事实、而非仅仅基于学术的传统与惯性来辩护，是可疑的。那个熟悉的叙事，是在现代政治出现期间演化出来的一系列道德故事的复合体。每一步的功能都是实用性的，即通过建构古代与中世纪的自由与专制模型，来为当下的政治立场辩护。被移置到专业史学中后，它们如今只是罗马史漫长进程的一个扭曲框架。对“本质性断裂”的信仰正普遍受到质疑。马修·卡内帕写道，“面对罗马文化中纷繁多样的变化，许多人屈服于一种诱惑，要通过为罗马史连续体中的边界发明名称来把它们实体化……遮蔽了罗马人对其文化连续性的感知。”
那些罗马人包括拜占庭人，他们对罗马史的连续性有强烈的信念。我们现在可以转向他们的证据。
en: It is doubtful that these labels and periodizations can be defended on the basis of source and facts rather than just the traditions and inertia of scholarship. The familiar narrative is a composite series of moral tales that evolved during the emergence of modern politics. The function of each step was pragmatic, namely, to defend political positions in the present by constructing ancient and medieval models of freedom and despotism. Transposed into professional historiography, they are now only a distorting framework for the long course of Roman history. The belief in “essential ruptures” is generally being questioned. Matthew Canepa has written that, “confronted by the great variety of changes in Roman culture, many have succumbed to a temptation to reify boundaries in the continuum of Roman history by inventing names for them... obscuring the Romans’ sense of the continuity of their culture.”
Those Romans included the Byzantines, who had a strong belief in the continuity of Roman history. It is to their evidence that we can now turn.

zh: 大概拜占庭没有人想恢复共和国，但许多人对罗马史的漫长进程感兴趣，那毕竟是他们自己的历史，而他们被共和国与君主制之间的过渡时期所吸引。值得听听他们对此说了什么，因为它揭示了他们如何理解其历史中底层的连续性。他们认为，无论治理形式如何更迭，作为基础的罗马政治共同体始终延续。结果发现，帝国早期的用希腊语写作的人比用拉丁语写作的人给出了一个更发达的论述，部分因为他们对旧共和国的形式没有忠诚，对君主制或
（“国王”）一词也没有反感。在拉丁方面，我们一般发现含糊的承认：
已经“改变”，有一个当前的、不同于“旧”的那个（正如我们在塔西佗那里所见）。
但普鲁塔克、阿庇安与卡西乌斯·狄奥等希腊作家（都是罗马人，尽管是帝国时期说希腊语的罗马人、因此是原初拜占庭人），作出了一个更微妙的观察：
已把其治理形式从共和国所是的那种（一种民主制？）变成了君主制。
en: Probably no one in Byzantium wanted to restore the Republic, but many were interested in the long run of Roman history, which was, after all, their own history, and they were drawn to the period of transition between the Republic and monarchy. It is worth listening to what they had to say about it because it reveals how they understood the underlying continuity in their history. What they believed was continuous was precisely the Roman polity that underlay regime-change. As it turns out, Greek writers of the early empire had given a more developed account of it than the Latin ones, in part because they had no loyalty to the forms of the old Republic and no aversion to monarchy or the word
(“king”). On the Latin side we generally find vague acknowledgments that the
had “changed,” that there was a current one different from the “old” one (as we saw in Tacitus).
But Greek writers such as Plutarch, Appianos, and Kassios Dion (all Romans, albeit Greek-speaking Romans of the empire and therefore proto-Byzantines), made a more subtle observation, that the
had changed its form of governance from whatever the Republic was (a democracy?) to a monarchy.

zh: 普鲁塔克声称，在内战的最后阶段“有许多人敢于说、甚至公开地说，
注定要灭亡，除非它能由一个君主制来保全。”
据阿庇安说，奥古斯都“胜过了他同时代的人，掌握了权力并使之安全稳定；他保全了
的形式与名称，却把自己确立为凌驾于一切之上的君主。而这种政府形式一直延续到此时，即在一个统治者之下。”
阿庇安后来说，恺撒被那些“渴望祖先的
”的人刺杀，
这大概指的是其
，因为他后来说“
为罗马人历经各种内战而存续下来，最终达成共识，走向君主制。”
卡西乌斯·狄奥关于共和国终结与君主制兴起的叙事，是现存最长的，也是从政治理论立场看最精致的。虽然对他来说罗马人的
也在帝国之下延续，他却呈现了一个更复杂的政体更替序列，从
（民主制），到
（军阀统治），最后到
（君主制）。狄奥提供了关于罗马“政权更迭”最有力的阐述，并被后来的拜占庭作家所追随，我们将会看到。他的最终裁决是“以这种方式，
被改革得更好、变得更安全；无论如何，在先前的民主制下他们不可能安全。”
对他来说，奥古斯都通过把民主制与君主制结合起来，确立了秩序并保全了罗马人的自由。
en: Plutarch claims that during the last phase of civil war “there were many who were daring to say, even openly, that the
was doomed unless it could be preserved by a monarchy.”
According to Appianos, Augustus “prevailed over the men of his time, took hold of power and made it safe and secure; he preserved the form and name of the
but established himself as a monarch over all. And this form of government has lasted until this time, namely under one ruler.”
Appianos later says that Caesar was assassinated by men who “longed for the ancestral
which presumably refers to its
for later he says that “the
survived for the Romans through the various civil wars to reach a point of consensus and monarchy.”
Kassios Dion’s narrative of the end of the Republic and the rise of the monarchy is the longest that survives and the most sophisticated from the standpoint of political theory. While for him too the
of the Romans carried on under the empire, he presents a more complex succession of regimes, from a
to a

Dion offered the most powerful exposition of “regime-change” at Rome, and was followed by later Byzantine writers, as we will see. His final verdict was that “in this way the
was reformed for the better and it became more secure; in any case, it would have been impossible for them to be safe under the previous democracy.”
Augustus, for him, established order and preserved the freedom of Romans by combining democracy with monarchy.

zh: 罗马史的漫长进程被想象和理论化为一个连续政体的历史，而治理形式间或发生宪制上的变化。这样做而无需公开讨论奥古斯都治下发生的那次过渡，是可能的。例如，哈利卡纳苏斯的狄奥尼修斯把政权更迭作为其
的主题之一，只是在这里他以希腊的方式使用
这个术语，来指罗马曾借以治理的不同政体类型。
他的讨论与希腊宪制理论相衔接（例如希罗多德笔下波斯人之间的辩论）。卡西乌斯·狄奥中的宪制辩论实际上置于同一传统之中，只是狄奥——一位罗马元老——把
理解为

en: The long course of Roman history was imagined and theorized as the history of one continuous polity punctuated by constitutional changes in the form of its governance. It was possible to do this without openly discussing the transition that took place under Augustus. For example, Dionysios of Halikarnassos made regime-change one of the main themes of his
only here he used the term
in the Greek way, to refer to the different types of regimes by which Rome had been governed.

His discussion linked up with Greek constitutional theory (e.g., the debate in Herodotos among the Persians). The constitutional debate in Kassios Dion is effectively set in the same tradition, only Dion, a Roman senator, understood
as the
not as its specific regime at any moment.

zh: 现在转向拜占庭证据，一系列文本揭示，中期作家以同样的方式看待从共和国向君主制的过渡，也就是说，他们把“罗马人的
”视为一个连续体，从罗慕路斯之后诸王的时代一直延伸到他们自己时代的拜占庭皇帝；只是政体类型改变了（在君主制确立时变得更好）。他们常把共和国称为“罗马由执政官统治的时代”。这方面的详细论证可以在六世纪作家、尤其是佐西莫斯与约安尼斯·吕多斯那里找到，
但我略过他们，聚焦于拜占庭中期的作家。
en: Turning now to the Byzantine evidence, a range of texts reveal that writers of the middle period viewed the transition from Republic to monarchy in the same way, that is, they regarded “the

of the Romans” as a continuum stretching from the time of the kings after Romulus down to the Byzantine emperor of their own time; only the type of regime changed (for the better in the establishment of monarchy). They often refer to the Republic as “the time when Rome was ruled by the consuls.” Detailed arguments to this effect can be found in writers of the sixth century, especially Zosimos and Ioannes Lydos,
but I pass them by to focus on writers of the middle Byzantine period.

zh: • 乔治·辛凯洛斯（约800年）：恺撒“来到罗马，废除了自塔克文·苏佩布以来一路相承的执政官治权；他是第一个作为君主统治罗马人的人，变得比任何曾作为国王在位者都更仁慈。”
又说：“后来的罗马皇帝以尤利乌斯·恺撒之名被称为恺撒，以奥古斯都之名被称为奥古斯都。在他治下
达到了顶点。”
en: • Georgios Synkellos (ca. 800): Caesar, “coming to Rome, dissolved the power of the consuls which had held sway in a direct line from Tarquinius Superbus; he was the first to rule as a monarch over the Romans, becoming more benevolent than any who had ever reigned as king.”
And: “later Roman emperors were named Caesars after Julius Caesar and Augusti after Augustus. Under him the
reached its apogee.”

of the Romans in its royal form lasted after the founding of Rome for 244 years. It became a tyranny under the last king Tarquinius and was dissolved by most noble men. With the end of the monarchy, or kingship, the state became an aristocracy.”

zh: • 1070年代，约安尼斯·西菲利诺斯为卡西乌斯·狄奥作了一个摘要，当他写到公元前27年的“宪制安排”时，他用自己的声音插入了以下话：“我现在将按必要的程度叙述每一事件，尤其从这一点往后，因为我们自己的生活与
完全取决于那时发生的事。我现在说这话，不再是作为生活在塞维鲁与亚历山大皇帝治下的普鲁萨的狄奥，而是作为约安尼斯·西菲利诺斯，牧首约安尼斯的侄子，我，在米海尔·杜卡斯皇帝治下编纂狄奥许多卷书的这个摘要。”
en: • In the 1070s, Ioannes Xiphilinos made an epitome of Kassios Dion and, when he reached the “constitutional settlement” of 27 BC, he interjected the following in his own voice: “I will now recount each event to the degree that it is necessary, especially from this point on, because our own lives and

序言中，佐纳拉斯列举了他后来在叙事中讨论的罗马所有政权更迭：“塔克文·苏佩布把王政变成僭主制后被废黜……然后罗马人的
]转向贵族制、再转向民主制，即执政官与独裁官的民主制，然后保民官治理
的行政……再后来从这种事态出发，罗马人的政治权力转向了君主制。”
在后面一卷，评论《但以理书》中诸王国的序列时，他考虑了与罗马不同政体相关的各种可能性，先是罗马由执政官治理时，后来是
变成君主制时。他指出内乱确实损害了

en: • Ioannes Zonaras (mid-twelfth century): in the preface to his
Zonaras lists all the regime changes at Rome that he later discusses in his narrative: “Tarquinius Superbus, having turned the kingship into a tyranny, was deposed... then the

... and later from this state of affairs political power was turned for the Romans into a monarchy.”

In a later book, commenting on the sequence of kingdoms in the book of Daniel, he considers various possibilities relating to different regimes at Rome, first when Rome was governed by the consuls and later when the
had become a monarchy. He notes that civil strife did harm to the
making the contemporary relevance of all this clear with a νῦν.

en: Similar expositions are found in later Byzantine sources.

zh: 这里不是讨论拜占庭人对其民族过去之看法、以及他们作为罗马人之身份的地方。我引述这些段落，只是为了表明：他们把从诸王到共和国、再到君主制的过渡，理解为单一
——内部的政权更迭，并以治理官职来识别不同阶段。与现代学术不同，他们毫不怀疑一个单一
的连续历史延伸到他们自己的当下，而且他们能够、也确实追溯了那段历史中的每一步。他们认为
在理论上先于在任何特定时刻统治它的那种特定政体类型。现在仍有待表明：他们对这个政体的构想，即便在其君主阶段，事实上也是上面所解释的那种意义上的“共和的”。
en: This is not the place to discuss the Byzantines’ view of their national past and their identity as Romans. I cite these passages only to show that they perceived the transition from the kings to the Republic and then to the monarchy in terms of regime change within a single
the
and identified the different phases by their governing offices. Unlike modern scholarship they had no doubt that a continuous history of a single
extended to their own present, and they could and did trace every step in that history. They thought of the

as theoretically prior to the specific type of regime that ruled it at any particular time. It remains to show now that their conception of this polity, even in its monarchical phase, was in fact “republican” in the sense explained above.
